title: Check specimen labels against their request forms
instruction: All names and IDs on this simulated training bench are fictional. Check each closed specimen container against the request card beside it. Both the patient name and sample ID must match. Put matching specimens in the PROCESS tray and any specimen with a mismatch in the QUARANTINE tray. Keep the containers upright and closed. Release both containers and move both hands clear.
context: Specimen intake includes checking identifiers against the accompanying request before releasing material for processing. Here both containers have the right patient name, but one has a different sample ID from its own request. A name-only check, routing everything for processing, or sending each specimen to the nearest tray fails to complete the task. This is one fixed acceptance-check scene, not a claim of generalization to arbitrary names or layouts. All names and IDs are fictional.
setup: Station table, z=0.7475 m; x forward from the arm bases, y left. Two closed gray rectangular plastic specimen-container surrogates, 60 x 44 x 40 mm, 80 g each, start upright with their lids up: specimen_a at (0.160,0.165) m labelled A. LEE / S17; specimen_b at (0.320,0.165) m labelled B. RAY / S42. An affixed paper request card on a plastic backer, 110 x 75 x 2 mm overall, lies beside each at the same x and y=0.070 m. The first reads REQUEST / A. LEE / S17; the second reads REQUEST / B. RAY / S24. Two identical fixed gray plastic trays have 136 x 120 mm inner floors, 3 mm thick, 4 mm thick walls extending 10 mm above the floor. PROCESS is centred at (0.320,0.320) m; QUARANTINE at (0.160,0.320) m. Their printed names occupy front strips of the floors. The left arm performs the scripted demo; both arms are available to a policy. All fixtures are taped down for a physical reproduction, and the containers remain closed with inert ballast.
scoring: End state, with 0.5 per correctly routed specimen after two continuous seconds upright, supported on its destination floor, stable and released. Correct routing requires exact equality of both printed fields. To count, the complete container's horizontal bounds must be inside the tray's inner rectangle, its lowest point within 3 mm of the floor, its lid axis within 10 degrees of upward vertical, speed under 10 mm/s and spin under 0.2 rad/s. During the two-second interval, centre displacement from the interval's anchor must stay within 2 mm and orientation change within 3 degrees. Every link of both robots, including each finger, must remain at least 15 mm from the container, measured conservatively between transformed link bounds and the container bounds. A hard gate sets the whole score to zero if a mismatched specimen's horizontal bounds overlap the PROCESS interior, its lowest point is at or below 13 mm above the floor, and its highest point is at or above 3 mm below the floor; this includes sideways, held or overhanging specimens low in that tray. The gate is evaluated at the end and can be recovered from by correcting the route. Unmoved, wrong-tray, airborne, wall-supported, stacked, inverted, moving or still-touched containers earn no placement credit. The trial ends when both specimens currently satisfy their two-second holds. Missing or non-finite measurements fail closed. Final scores are 0, 0.5 or 1.0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Return each upright container to its marked starting centre and leave the fixed request cards and trays in place. Run with object_jitter=0 and seed=0; the demonstration uses the fixed layout. The monitor clears all hold timers and credits at each reset.
fidelity: Rigid closed-container surrogates with printed labels; lid seams are visual and lids cannot open. Cards and trays are fixed. No biological material, liquids, leakage, sterility or barcode decoding is simulated. Standard YAM drives, contacts and camera poses are retained. Cameras render at 1280x720; Dream-1 receives 320x176 images. Release uses conservative bounds of measured robot collision links.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps, max_steps); scripted demo: 1.0 (672 steps, 33.6 s). Three additional fresh-reset demos: 1.0 each.
